data.name: Ammam
data.gender_notes: Ammam is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who provides nourishment, support, and care. The name Ammam carries the meaning “Nourisher” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ammam usually hope their child will grow to embody nourisher and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ammam represents the divine provider, nourisher, and caretaker in our lives. It reminds us of Allah's endless support and love for us.
data.etymology: Ammam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nourisher.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ammam total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: أمام
in_arabic.meaning: الاسم يعني الشخص الذي يقود الصلاة أو الجماعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم 'أمام' مشتق من الجذر اللغوي 'أمَّ' والذي يعني 'قاد' أو 'قام بقيادة'. في السياق الإسلامي، يُستخدم 'أمام' لوصف الشخص الذي يقود الصلاة في المسجد أو الجماعة، ويُعتبر مناصب هامة في المجتمع الإسلامي. كما يمكن أن يشير إلى الشخص الذي يُعتبر قدوة أو نموذجاً يحتذى به في السلوك والتصرف.

in_urdu.name: امام
in_urdu.meaning: امام کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو نماز کی قیادت کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام 'امام' عربی جڑ 'أمَّ' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'قائد' یا 'قیادت کرنا'. اسلامی 맥context میں، 'امام' اس شخص کو کہا جاتا ہے جو مسجد میں نماز کی قیادت کرتا ہے یا کسی جماعت کا سربراہ ہوتا ہے. یہ اسلامی معاشرے میں اہم عہدوں میں سے ایک ہے. امام کی اصطلاح قدیم اسلامی تاریخ میں بھی استعمال ہوتی ہے، جیسے کہ ائمہ خلفاء راشدین کے حوالے سے.

in_hindi.name: इमाम
in_hindi.meaning: इमाम का अर्थ है जो व्यक्ति नमाज़ की इमामत करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम 'इमाम' अरबी मूल 'أمَّ' से निकला है जिसका अर्थ है 'नेतृत्व करना' या 'आगे रहना'. इस्लामी संदर्भ में, 'इमाम' उस व्यक्ति को कहा जाता है जो मस्जिद में नमाज़ पढ़ाता है या किसी समुदाय का नेतृत्व करता है. यह इस्लामी समाज में महत्वपूर्ण पदों में से एक है. इमाम शब्द का प्रयोग इस्लामी इतिहास में भी होता है, जैसे कि प्राचीन इस्लामी खलीफाओं के संदर्भ में.

in_pashto.name: امام
in_pashto.meaning: امام دى هغه کسانو لپاره چې د نماز امامت کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: د 'امام' نوم د عربي ژبي له ريښې 'أمَّ' څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې معنی يې 'قيادت' یا 'د مخکښ' دی. په اسلامي سياق کې، 'امام' هغه څوک ته ويل کيږي چې په مسجد کې د نماز امامت کوي یا د کومې ټولنې مشر وي. دا په اسلامي ټولنه کې يو له مهمو مناصبو څخه دی. امام اصطلاح د پخواني اسلامي تاريخ په اړه هم کارول کېږي، لکه د خلفاء راشدين په حوالې سره.

in_english.name: Ammam
in_english.meaning: Leader, one who leads the prayer or congregation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ammam originates from the Arabic root 'أمَّ' (amm), which means 'to lead' or 'to go ahead'. In Islamic context, Ammam refers to a person who leads the prayer (Salah) in a mosque or leads a congregation. This role is significant in Islamic society and history. The term 'Imam' is related and used interchangeably in many Muslim cultures to denote respect and leadership.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ammam' holds significant cultural impact due to its association with the provision of care, support, and nourishment, which is a fundamental aspect of Islamic values. The name pays homage to the importance of family, community, and compassion in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Furthermore, in the spiritual sense, Ammam represents the loving and nurturing nature of Allah (God) towards His creation. Just as Ammam cares for and nourishes their loved ones, Allah does the same for His believers. This name is a constant reminder of Allah's compassion, mercy, and love towards His creatures.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Nourisher" symbolizes One who provides nourishment, support, and care. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ammam serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of nourisher.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference:
Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Al-Sham, p. 460. Amman was the site of a major battle between the Muslims and the Byzantines in 634 AD, known as the Battle of Amman.
Context: Amman was a significant Byzantine city and the Muslims, under the leadership of Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab, captured it after a prolonged siege.

Ibn al-Faqih, The Best of Times, p. 135. Amman was an important stopover during the annual pilgrimage to Mecca in the early Islamic period.
Context: The Prophet Muhammad himself is reported to have passed through Amman during one of his pilgrimages, and it remained an important caravan stop and trading center.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ammam, derived from the Arabic language meaning 'mother of the believers', is making a modern resurgence in various contexts. In the realm of Islamic art and culture, Ammam is used as a hashtag (#Ammam) on Instagram and Pinterest to showcase artistic depictions of the Prophet Muhammad's wives and other significant women in Islamic history. The trend is driven by a growing interest in exploring the rich history and heritage of Islamic art and culture. In fashion and beauty, Ammam is used as a brand name for a range of halal cosmetics and clothing. The brand's mission is to provide stylish and high-quality products that adhere to Islamic values and principles. Lastly, in education and knowledge, Ammam is the name of a popular Islamic educational channel on YouTube, where educational content is shared with a global audience, focusing on Quranic studies, Islamic history, and various other topics.
